evals.prompt: ROS 2 Jazzy is already installed on Ubuntu 24.04. Clone and build IsaacSim-ros_workspaces.
evals.expected_output: Selects the native Jazzy workflow, installs only missing workspace dependencies, resolves rosdep dependencies, and runs colcon in jazzy_ws.
assertions: The agent identified isaac-sim-ros-workspaces as the primary skill without being told its name
Prefers native ROS because a matching installation is present
Does not install a public ROS 2 distribution
Skips apt and sudo when native workspace build tools and rosdep sources are already available
Uses setup_ros_workspace.sh with native or automatic method selection
Does not require the user to pre-export DEBIAN_FRONTEND or PIP_BREAK_SYSTEM_PACKAGES
Builds jazzy_ws and prints its local_setup.bash path

evals.prompt: Set up the Isaac Sim ROS workspace on Ubuntu 24.04. ROS 2 is not installed.
evals.expected_output: Falls back to the prebuilt-image Docker Jazzy workspace build without installing ROS 2.
assertions: The agent chooses the Docker workspace method because matching native ROS is absent
Uses osrf/ros:jazzy-desktop on x86_64 or arm64v8/ros:jazzy on aarch64
Does not route to a ROS installation skill
Does not use build_ros.sh unless custom interfaces or Python 3.12 were requested

evals.prompt: Build IsaacSim-ros_workspaces on Ubuntu 24.04. The ros2 command is not on PATH, but /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash exists.
evals.expected_output: Treats Jazzy as installed but unsourced and lets setup_ros_workspace.sh select the native workflow.
assertions: The agent does not conclude ROS 2 is absent from which ros2 or command -v ros2
The agent recognizes /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash as the matching native installation
The agent uses setup_ros_workspace.sh with native or automatic method selection
The agent does not switch to Docker solely because ros2 is not on PATH

evals.prompt: Build jazzy_ws inside a Docker container on my x86_64 Linux host.
evals.expected_output: Uses the prebuilt osrf/ros:jazzy-desktop image and builds the mounted jazzy_ws with rosdep and colcon.
assertions: The agent selects the container workspace build, not the custom-interface build
Pulls osrf/ros:jazzy-desktop
Initializes submodules on the host before running the container
Runs rosdep and colcon in the mounted workspace

evals.prompt: On an Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 DGX Spark without ROS installed, build the Isaac Sim Jazzy workspace.
evals.expected_output: Uses the aarch64 Jazzy ROS image and performs the Docker workspace build.
assertions: The agent detects aarch64 and chooses arm64v8/ros:jazzy
Does not pull the x86_64 osrf/ros:jazzy-desktop image
Uses the Docker workspace build rather than build_ros.sh

evals.prompt: Build the Humble custom ROS interfaces so Isaac Sim's Python 3.12 runtime can import them on Ubuntu 22.04.
evals.expected_output: Runs the cloned repository's build_ros.sh for Humble and reports both Python 3.12 workspace outputs.
assertions: The agent selects the custom-interface workflow
Runs build_ros.sh -d humble -v 22.04 from the cloned repository root
Requires Docker but does not use a prebuilt ROS desktop image as the workflow entrypoint
Reports build_ws/humble/humble_ws and build_ws/humble/isaac_sim_ros_ws

evals.prompt: Build my custom Jazzy messages in Docker for Isaac Sim Python 3.12 on Ubuntu 22.04.
evals.expected_output: Treats custom-interface intent as higher priority than generic Docker wording and invokes build_ros.sh.
assertions: The agent selects custom rather than the prebuilt-image Docker workspace method
Runs build_ros.sh -d jazzy -v 22.04
Explains that this path builds Python 3.12-compatible interfaces

evals.prompt: Set up and build IsaacSim-ros_workspaces on Windows 11 x64.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Windows Jazzy Pixi workflow after checking Windows, MSVC, winget, Git, and Pixi.
assertions: The agent selects Windows Jazzy Pixi without asking for a ROS installation
Invokes setup_pixi_workspace.ps1 with powershell.exe -File rather than inventing Bash-wrapped PowerShell prerequisite one-liners
Does not conclude MSVC is missing from a single-quoted ${env:ProgramFiles(x86)} path probe
Relies on the script for Windows, MSVC, winget, Git, and Pixi gates
Runs pixi install and pixi run build in jazzy_ws

evals.prompt: Setup the Isaac Sim ROS workspace on Windows 11. First check whether MSVC Build Tools are installed using ${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the fragile env-expansion probe and runs setup_pixi_workspace.ps1 so the script owns the MSVC gate.
assertions: The agent does not trust a Bash-wrapped single-quoted ${env:ProgramFiles(x86)} Test-Path result
The agent runs setup_pixi_workspace.ps1 with powershell.exe -File
If a manual path check is used at all, it uses the literal C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe path
The agent does not stop solely because an invented env-expansion probe returned false

evals.prompt: Explicitly use Pixi to build IsaacSim-ros_workspaces on Ubuntu 22.04.
evals.expected_output: Installs Pixi when needed and builds humble_ws through its Pixi project.
assertions: The agent honors the explicit Linux Pixi request
Selects Humble for Ubuntu 22.04
Checks for humble_ws/pixi.toml before running Pixi
Runs pixi install and pixi run build from humble_ws

evals.prompt: Clone branch release/6.0 from https://git.example.internal/robotics/ros-workspaces.git and build it with my installed Jazzy.
evals.expected_output: Passes the internal URL and branch to the native workspace setup without replacing them with the public repository.
assertions: The agent preserves the user-provided repository URL
Passes release/6.0 as the clone branch
Selects native Jazzy because the prompt states it is installed
Does not expose or request credentials in command arguments

evals.prompt: ROS is absent and Docker is not installed. Build the Isaac Sim Jazzy workspace.
evals.expected_output: Stops at the Docker prerequisite gate with Docker CE and group-session remediation.
assertions: The agent does not install Docker automatically
The agent does not install public ROS 2
The response instructs the user to install Docker CE and retry
The response mentions re-login or newgrp docker when group membership changes

evals.prompt: Build the workspace natively from a non-interactive agent session. ROS Jazzy is installed, but colcon is missing and sudo requires a password.
evals.expected_output: Stops before clone/build and prints exact interactive package-install or sudo pre-authentication instructions.
assertions: The agent does not hang waiting for a sudo password
The agent identifies the missing native build dependency before invoking apt
The response provides exact sudo install commands or instructs the user to run sudo -v interactively
The agent does not switch to Docker without the user requesting a method change

evals.prompt: Set up the Isaac Sim ROS workspace. The target path already contains a checkout on develop with local changes.
evals.expected_output: Asks whether to reuse the existing checkout or create a clean clone before running the setup script.
assertions: The agent explains that a clean clone deletes local and untracked changes
The agent asks one focused reuse-or-clean question before running the setup script
The agent does not switch, reset, delete, or clean the checkout automatically
If reuse is selected, the agent passes develop as the branch and does not pass a clean-reclone flag

evals.prompt: Delete the existing C:\IsaacSim-ros_workspaces Git checkout, including my local changes, and make a clean clone of branch main on Windows 11.
evals.expected_output: Treats the destructive intent as explicit and invokes the Windows setup script with -CleanReclone and -YesIKnow.
assertions: The agent uses powershell.exe -File to run setup_pixi_workspace.ps1
The agent passes -CleanReclone, -YesIKnow, -Branch main, and the exact repository path
The agent does not run a separate Remove-Item command
The agent relies on the script to reject unsafe, non-Git, symbolic-link, or reparse-point paths

evals.prompt: Build humble_ws for Isaac Sim on Ubuntu 24.04.
evals.expected_output: Uses the prebuilt Humble Docker image because native Humble is unsupported on Ubuntu 24.04.

Does not change the requested distro to Jazzy

evals.prompt: Build jazzy_ws for Isaac Sim on Ubuntu 22.04.
evals.expected_output: Uses the prebuilt Jazzy Docker image because native Jazzy is unsupported on Ubuntu 22.04.

The agent selects the Docker method with --distro jazzy
Uses osrf/ros:jazzy-desktop on x86_64 or arm64v8/ros:jazzy on aarch64
Does not change the requested distro to Humble

evals.prompt: Build the Humble Isaac Sim ROS workspace natively on Ubuntu 24.04.
evals.expected_output: Rejects native Humble on Ubuntu 24.04 and points the user to the Docker method instead.
assertions: The agent does not attempt the unsupported native build
The agent identifies Docker as the supported path for Humble on Ubuntu 24.04
The agent does not silently change the requested distro to Jazzy and build natively

The agent states that Windows Pixi supports Jazzy only
